collection.description: The whole village is gathered for the feast, and the food is piled high on banana leaves all around the fire.

ask.text:
The whole village is gathered for the feast, and the food is piled high on banana leaves all around the fire. In the middle of the laughter and chatter, (subject) notices something odd. There's an extra place set at the end of the row: a fresh banana leaf heaped with food and a cup of coconut milk. Nobody is sitting there.
"Who set that?" (subject) asks. Nobody knows. Nobody remembers doing it. And every time (subject) looks back at it, there's a little less food on the leaf than before. What should (subject.he/she) do?

c1o1.text: The feast goes on late into the night. In the morning, the extra leaf is spotless, licked clean, and the cup is dry. Nobody saw anyone eat. Nobody heard a thing. The villagers quietly wonder about it for a long time, and at the next feast, without anyone saying a word, somebody sets an extra place again.

c1o2.text: Later in the evening, (child), very small and very sticky, is found sitting behind the cooking pots with an entire mango in each hand and a coconut-milk moustache. (Child) had set the extra place "for the spirits" and then got hungry waiting for them. (Child) looks extremely guilty. Everyone laughs until they cry, and (child) gets a second mango.

c2o1.text: For a moment, everything goes quiet. Then a soft, warm breeze passes through the gathering, stirring hair and leaves, and every torch around the feast flares up brighter, all at once. People gasp, then cheer. It's the best feast anyone can remember, and nobody can quite explain why everyone feels so happy.

c2o2.text: "Thank you," says a voice from the dark, and a tired traveler steps hesitantly into the firelight. The traveler had been standing at the edge of the trees for an hour, too shy to ask to join. The traveler gratefully takes the empty seat, eats every scrap, and tells funny stories until the fire dies. Nobody ever finds out who set the place.

c3o1.text: For ages, nothing. Then (subject) glances away for half a second, and there's a flapping of leathery wings: a fruit bat swoops down from the trees, grabs a whole mango off the leaf and flaps off into the night, squeaking with triumph. (subject) leaps up, shouting. Everyone laughs. It's been doing it all evening, apparently.

c3o2.text: (subject) points it out, and soon the whole feast is watching the empty seat in silence. And as everyone watches, the food simply... goes. A little at a time. Bite by bite, it vanishes, until the leaf is bare and the cup is empty. No hands. No mouth. Nothing. Nobody says anything for a long time. Then somebody starts the drums again, a bit too loudly.
